name: Si Ji Chun
parentage: Natural cross-pollination of Wu Yi and Qing Xin Gan Zhi.
description: 'Four Seasons Spring'. A famously prolific and aromatic cultivar, discovered as a natural cross in the 1980s. It's named for its ability to be harvested almost year-round, while still producing a tea with an explosive, forward, and highly accessible floral aroma, primarily of gardenia and jasmine.
plantType: Extremely vigorous, dense, and highly productive bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Thrives in lower-altitude, warmer, and more humid climates, which allows for its near-constant flushing and harvesting.
processing: Processing is fast and efficient, aimed at capturing the cultivar's potent upfront aroma. It is a workhorse cultivar that responds well to standard green oolong processing.
oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light (10-20%) to ensure the final product is dominated by the fresh, powerful gardenia and jasmine notes.
roasting: Unroasted. Its value lies in its fresh floral aroma, which would be destroyed by any significant roasting.
versatility: Low versatility. While incredibly productive, it is a specialist in producing one type of tea: a fragrant, accessible, and affordable light oolong. It lacks the structure for other styles.

taiwan: Nantou County (Mingjian is the largest area)

Oolong Tea (Aromatic Style).Si Ji Chun Oolong: Almost always made as a very lightly oxidized, unroasted oolong (often in the twisted Baozhong style) to maximize its powerful, fresh floral aroma. It's a popular daily-drinker tea.

sensory.aroma: Intense, forward Gardenia, Jasmine, and other white flowers
sensory.flavor: Crisp, highly floral, and slightly pungent with a brisk finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Light-to-medium-bodied with a fresh, clean texture. The liquor is a pale green-yellow.
